\\\"Only sessions with at least 400 trials were retained\\\" |\\n| Neural data time bin | **20 ms**, T = **100** | \\\"Recordings are split into 2-s trials, each divided into 20-ms bins, producing T = 100 time steps\\\" |\\n| Behaviour sampling | 60 Hz (left cam) | \\\"wheel speed and whisker motion energy are time-varying signals sampled at 60 Hz\\\" |\\n| Alignment for choice | stimulus onset, −0.5 → +1.5 s | \\\"For choice, we align trials to the stimulus onset, considering neural activity from 0.5 s before to 1.5 s post-onset\\\" |\\n| Reward rate | ~0.85 (measured on example session) | task performance ≥90% on 100% contrast trials |\\n| Block structure | first 90 trials at 0.5; then 0.2/0.8 blocks of 20–100 trials, mean 51 | \\\"After an initial 90 unbiased trials… empirical mean of 51 trials\\\" |\\n| Contrast set | {0, 6.25, 12.5, 25, 100}% | data paper |\\n| Choice decoding (Zhang, region `all`) | AUC 0.90 (all units) / 0.87 (good units) | example decoder outputs |\\n| Prior decoding (Zhang, region `all`) | R² 0.27 / 0.18 | example decoder outputs |\\n\\n### Processing Details\\n- **Alignment**: `stimOn_times`, window `(-0.5, +1.5) s` ⇒ 2 s interval.\\n- **Binning**: 20 ms non-overlapping ⇒ T = 100. Spike bin `k` spans\\n  `[stimOn − 0.5 + 0.02k, stimOn − 0.5 + 0.02(k+1))` (this is exactly what `bincount2D`\\n  with `xlim=[t_beg,t_end]` does, and the reference then truncates to the first 100 columns).\\n- **Continuous behaviour**: linearly interpolated onto `t_beg + 0.02·(k+1)`, i.e. the **right edge**\\n  of each spike bin.\\n- The method paper also describes 50-ms bins in a −0.5/+1.5 s window for choice and a\\n  movement-aligned 0/+1 s window for the dynamic behaviours; the *released caching code*\\n  (which is what is reproducible and which produces one dataset carrying all four behaviours)\\n  uses the stimulus-onset 2 s / 20 ms / T=100 configuration, which is also the configuration\\n  stated in the paper's Results (\\\"2-s trials… 20-ms bins… T = 100\\\"). The Decoder Task here\\n  fixes stimulus-onset alignment, so that configuration is used.\\n\\n### Curation Steps\\n\\n**Neuron curation rules** (data paper \\\"Neurons and brain regions\\\"):\\n- Exclude units failing any of the three RIGOR single-unit metrics: amplitude > 50 µV,\\n  noise cut-off < 20 µV, refractory-period violation. Units passing all three are\\n  \\\"well-isolated neurons\\\" (75,708 of 621,733). In the IBL cluster table this is exactly\\n  `label >= 1` (`label` is the fraction of the three metrics passed: 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1).\\n- Analyses further restricted to **grey-matter** regions in the Allen CCF, with ≥5 neurons\\n  per session and recorded in ≥2 sessions.\\n\\n**Trial curation rules** (data paper \\\"Trials\\\", implemented in `load_trials_and_mask`):\\n- Exclude a trial if any of `stimOn_times`, `choice`, `feedback_times`, `probabilityLeft`,\\n  `firstMovement_times`, `feedbackType` is NaN.\\n- Exclude if reaction time (`firstMovement_times − stimOn_times`) ∉ [0.08, 2.00] s.\\n- Reference code adds `max_trial_len=10.0` (`feedback_times − goCue_times ≤ 10 s`) and\\n  `exclude_nochoice=True` (`choice != 0`).\\n\\n### Decoders Trained (reference)\\n| Decoded variable | Metric | Reference value (region `all`) |\\n|------------------|--------|-------------------------------|\\n| choice | AUC | 0.896 (all units) / 0.869 (good units) |\\n| prior | R² | 0.270 / 0.182 |\\n| wheel speed | R² | reported only in figures (single-trial R², ≈0.4–0.6) |\\n| whisker motion energy | R² | reported only in figures (≈0.5–0.7) |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Step 4: Check for Consistency\\n**Status**: COMPLETE\\n\\n### Discrepancies Found\\n| Topic | Code says | Data shows | Papers say | Resolution |\\n|-------|-----------|------------|------------|------------|\\n| Neuron quality filter | `load_spiking_data(qc=None)` ⇒ **all** Kilosort clusters | `label>=1` selects ~8–15% of clusters (76/898, 264/1728, 163/1202) | Method paper: \\\"bin spike counts using **all neurons**, sorted by Kilosort 2.5\\\"; data paper: analyses restricted to the **75,708 well-isolated neurons** | **Use well-isolated neurons (`label >= 1`)**. Rationale below. |\\n| Brain-region set | `list_brain_regions` keeps every Beryl acronym incl. `root`/`void`; `MultiRegionDataModule` drops `root`/`void` | 15–20% of good clusters map to `root`/`void` | Data paper restricts to Allen **grey matter** | Drop `root`/`void` (non-grey-matter / unassigned), keep everything else. Gives a Beryl region list comparable to the paper's 270 regions. |\\n| Time bin | code: 20 ms, T=100 | — | Results: 20 ms, T=100; STAR Methods \\\"data processing\\\": 50 ms for choice/prior, 20 ms for dynamic behaviours | Use **20 ms, T = 100**: it matches the released code and the Results text, and the Decoder Task requires one common binning for all four outputs. |\\n| Alignment | code: `stimOn_times` | — | STAR Methods uses `firstMovement_times` for the dynamic behaviours | Use **`stimOn_times`** — mandated by the Decoder Task and by the released caching code. |\\n| `allow_nans` for behaviours | reference passes `allow_nans=True` and later imputes NaNs with the trial mean inside the data loader | motion energy occasionally has NaN runs | — | Drop trials whose wheel-speed or whisker-ME window contains NaN. The target format forbids NaN, and imputing a value then discretising it would fabricate labels. |\\n| Sessions | freeze file lists 459 eids | 461 session dirs staged | Method paper used **433** sessions | Start from the 459-eid freeze, drop sessions with no usable whisker video, no surviving neurons, or <2 usable trials; expect to land near 433. |\\n| `choice` sign | code stores raw `choice` | on 100%-contrast trials: stim-left ⇒ `choice=+1` in 71/72 trials, stim-right ⇒ `choice=−1` in 61/63 | mice report the stimulus side | `choice == +1` ⇒ **left** report ⇒ label 0; `choice == −1` ⇒ **right** report ⇒ label 1. |\\n\\n**Why well-isolated neurons rather than \\\"all neurons\\\":**\\n1. The data paper — the source of these data — explicitly defines its analysis population as the\\n   75,708 well-isolated neurons and excludes the rest as multi-unit activity.\\n2. The reference code exposes exactly this switch (`qc=1` ⇒ `label >= 1`) and its `merge_probes`\\n   docstring is written against `brainwidemap.load_good_units`.\\n3. Feasibility: all 621,733 units at T=100 × ~300 usable trials × 459 sessions would be ≈120 GB of\\n   float32 — not a storable/trainable dataset. Well-isolated units give ≈8 GB.\\n4. Cost is small and quantified: the reference's own example outputs show choice AUC 0.896 with\\n   all units vs 0.869 with good units (−3%).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Step 5: Mapping Planning\\n**Status**: COMPLETE\\n\\n### Variable Mapping\\n| Source Variable | Target Field | Transform | Reference Code Function(s) | Notes |\\n|-----------------|--------------|-----------|----------------------------|-------|\\n| `spikes.times`, `spikes.clusters` (all probes, merged) | `neural[s][k]` (n_neurons, 100) float32 | spike counts in 20 ms bins over `stimOn + [-0.5, 1.5)` | `merge_probes`, `bin_spiking_data`/`bincount2D` | raw counts, no rate conversion, no z-scoring (reference z-scores inside the model's data loader, not in the cached data) |\\n| bin right-edge time relative to `stimOn_times` | `input[s][k][0, :]` | `-0.5 + 0.02·(k+1)` ∈ [−0.48, 1.50] | `get_behavior_per_interval`'s `x_interp` grid | \\\"time since stimulus onset\\\", continuous, time-varying |\\n| index of the trial within its `probabilityLeft` block | `input[s][k][1, :]` | 0-based count from block start, computed on the **unfiltered** trials table, broadcast over T | — (new; required by Decoder Task) | \\\"trial number in block\\\", continuous, per-trial → broadcast to time-varying |\\n| `trials.choice` | `output[s][k][0, :]` | `+1 → 0` (left), `−1 → 1` (right); broadcast over T | `bin_behaviors` (`choice`) | binary, per-trial |\\n| `trials.probabilityLeft` | `output[s][k][1, :]` | `0.2→0, 0.5→1, 0.8→2`; broadcast over T | `bin_behaviors` (`block`) | 3-way, per-trial |\\n| `SessionLoader.wheel.velocity` | `output[s][k][2, :]` | `abs(velocity)` → interp to bin edges → per-session tertiles → {0,1,2} | `load_target_behavior('wheel-speed')`, `get_behavior_per_interval` | time-varying |\\n| `leftCamera.ROIMotionEnergy` (fallback `rightCamera`) | `output[s][k][3, :]` | interp to bin edges → per-session tertiles → {0,1,2} | `load_target_behavior('left-whisker-motion-energy')` | time-varying |\\n| `clusters.acronym` → Beryl | `brain_region_idx[s]`, `brain_regions` | `BrainRegions().acronym2acronym(..., 'Beryl')` | `list_brain_regions` | `root`/`void` dropped |\\n| `bwm_release.csv` `subject` | `subjects`, `subject_idx` | unique sorted list | — | |\\n\\n### Key Decisions\\n1. **Alignment / window / binning**: `stimOn_times`, `(-0.5, +1.5) s`, 20 ms ⇒ T = 100.\\n   Exactly the reference `params`; also required by the Decoder Task.\\n2. **Neuron curation**: IBL `label >= 1` (all three RIGOR metrics passed) **and** Beryl region\\n   ∉ {`root`, `void`}. Sessions are merged across probes first (`merge_probes`), as the reference\\n   and the data paper both do (\\\"neurons in the same session and region were combined across probes\\\").\\n   The data paper's extra region criteria (≥5 neurons/session, region seen in ≥2 sessions) are\\n   *not* applied: they exist to make region-wise statistical maps comparable, whereas here every\\n   session is decoded from its whole population, and applying them would delete neurons that\\n   carry signal for a session-level decoder.\\n3. **Trial curation**: `load_trials_and_mask(min_rt=0.08, max_rt=2.0, nan_exclude='default',\\n   max_trial_len=10.0, exclude_nochoice=True)` — the reference call verbatim — plus the\\n   reference's behaviour-coverage checks (`get_behavior_per_interval`), plus rejection of\\n   trials with NaN in either continuous behaviour.\\n4. **Neural values**: raw spike counts stored as float32 (matching the reference's `ubyte` CSR\\n   cache). Standardisation is a model-side step in the reference and the provided decoder does\\n   its own SVD projection.\\n5. **Discretisation of continuous outputs**: per-session tertiles (33.3 / 66.7 percentiles) of the\\n   binned values pooled over all retained trials of that session, giving classes\\n   `low`/`medium`/`high`. Per-session rather than global because whisker motion energy is in\\n   arbitrary units that depend on camera, illumination and ROI size and is therefore not\\n   comparable across sessions; tertiles because the Decoder Task asks for 3 bins and balanced\\n   accuracy is the evaluation metric, so equal-frequency bins are the natural choice.\\n6. **Everything time-varying**: `input` and `output` are both `(d, 100)` per trial; per-trial\\n   quantities are broadcast across time, as the format instructions prefer.\\n7. **Session exclusion**: sessions from the 459-eid BWM freeze; dropped if no whisker motion\\n   energy is available, if no neuron survives curation, or if fewer than 2 trials survive.\\n\\n### Planned Sanity Checks\\n- [ ] #sessions ≈ 433 (method paper), #subjects ≤ 139, Beryl regions ≈ 270\\n- [ ] mean good neurons/session ≈ 75,708 / 459 ≈ 165 before grey-matter filtering\\n- [ ] T == 100 for every trial; `input[0]` range == [−0.48, 1.50]\\n- [ ] choice class balance Spike bin `k` spans\\n  `[stimOn − 0.5 + 0.02k, stimOn − 0.5 + 0.02(k+1))` (this is exactly what `bincount2D`\\n  with `xlim=[t_beg,t_end]` does, and the reference then truncates to the first 100 columns).\\n- **Continuous behaviour**: linearly interpolated onto `t_beg + 0.02·(k+1)`, i.e. the **right edge**\\n  of each spike bin.\\n- The method paper also describes 50-ms bins in a −0.5/+1.5 s window for choice and a\\n  movement-aligned 0/+1 s window for the dynamic behaviours; the *released caching code*\\n  (which is what is reproducible and which produces one dataset carrying all four behaviours)\\n  uses the stimulus-onset 2 s / 20 ms / T=100 configuration, which is also the configuration\\n  stated in the paper's Results (\\\"2-s trials… 20-ms bins… T = 100\\\"). The Decoder Task here\\n  fixes stimulus-onset alignment, so that configuration is used.\\n\\n### Curation Steps\\n\\n**Neuron curation rules** (data paper \\\"Neurons and brain regions\\\"):\\n- Exclude units failing any of the three RIGOR single-unit metrics: amplitude > 50 µV,\\n  noise cut-off < 20 µV, refractory-period violation. Units passing all three are\\n  \\\"well-isolated neurons\\\" (75,708 of 621,733). In the IBL cluster table this is exactly\\n  `label >= 1` (`label` is the fraction of the three metrics passed: 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1).\\n- Analyses further restricted to **grey-matter** regions in the Allen CCF, with ≥5 neurons\\n  per session and recorded in ≥2 sessions.\\n\\n**Trial curation rules** (data paper \\\"Trials\\\", implemented in `load_trials_and_mask`):\\n- Exclude a trial if any of `stimOn_times`, `choice`, `feedback_times`, `probabilityLeft`,\\n  `firstMovement_times`, `feedbackType` is NaN.\\n- Exclude if reaction time (`firstMovement_times − stimOn_times`) ∉ [0.08, 2.00] s.\\n- Reference code adds `max_trial_len=10.0` (`feedback_times − goCue_times ≤ 10 s`) and\\n  `exclude_nochoice=True` (`choice != 0`).\\n\\n### Decoders Trained (reference)\\n| Decoded variable | Metric | Reference value (region `all`) |\\n|------------------|--------|-------------------------------|\\n| choice | AUC | 0.896 (all units) / 0.869 (good units) |\\n| prior | R² | 0.270 / 0.182 |\\n| wheel speed | R² | reported only in figures (single-trial R², ≈0.4–0.6) |\\n| whisker motion energy | R² | reported only in figures (≈0.5–0.7) |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Step 4: Check for Consistency\\n**Status**: COMPLETE\\n\\n### Discrepancies Found\\n| Topic | Code says | Data shows | Papers say | Resolution |\\n|-------|-----------|------------|------------|------------|\\n| Neuron quality filter | `load_spiking_data(qc=None)` ⇒ **all** Kilosort clusters | `label>=1` selects ~8–15% of clusters (76/898, 264/1728, 163/1202) | Method paper: \\\"bin spike counts using **all neurons**, sorted by Kilosort 2.5\\\"; data paper: analyses restricted to the **75,708 well-isolated neurons** | **Use well-isolated neurons (`label >= 1`)**. The reference code exposes exactly this switch (`qc=1` ⇒ `label >= 1`) and its `merge_probes`\\n   docstring is written against `brainwidemap.load_good_units`.\\n3. Feasibility: all 621,733 units at T=100 × ~300 usable trials × 459 sessions would be ≈120 GB of\\n   float32 — not a storable/trainable dataset. Well-isolated units give ≈8 GB.\\n4. Cost is small and quantified: the reference's own example outputs show choice AUC 0.896 with\\n   all units vs 0.869 with good units (−3%).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Step 5: Mapping Planning\\n**Status**: COMPLETE\\n\\n### Variable Mapping\\n| Source Variable | Target Field | Transform | Reference Code Function(s) | Notes |\\n|-----------------|--------------|-----------|----------------------------|-------|\\n| `spikes.times`, `spikes.clusters` (all probes, merged) | `neural[s][k]` (n_neurons, 100) float32 | spike counts in 20 ms bins over `stimOn + [-0.5, 1.5)` | `merge_probes`, `bin_spiking_data`/`bincount2D` | raw counts, no rate conversion, no z-scoring (reference z-scores inside the model's data loader, not in the cached data) |\\n| bin right-edge time relative to `stimOn_times` | `input[s][k][0, :]` | `-0.5 + 0.02·(k+1)` ∈ [−0.48, 1.50] | `get_behavior_per_interval`'s `x_interp` grid | \\\"time since stimulus onset\\\", continuous, time-varying |\\n| index of the trial within its `probabilityLeft` block | `input[s][k][1, :]` | 0-based count from block start, computed on the **unfiltered** trials table, broadcast over T | — (new; also required by the Decoder Task.\\n2. **Neuron curation**: IBL `label >= 1` (all three RIGOR metrics passed) **and** Beryl region\\n   ∉ {`root`, `void`}. Sessions are merged across probes first (`merge_probes`), as the reference\\n   and the data paper both do (\\\"neurons in the same session and region were combined across probes\\\").\\n   The data paper's extra region criteria (≥5 neurons/session, region seen in ≥2 sessions) are\\n   *not* applied: they exist to make region-wise statistical maps comparable, whereas here every\\n   session is decoded from its whole population, and applying them would delete neurons that\\n   carry signal for a session-level decoder.\\n3. **Trial curation**: `load_trials_and_mask(min_rt=0.08, max_rt=2.0, nan_exclude='default',\\n   max_trial_len=10.0, exclude_nochoice=True)` — the reference call verbatim — plus the\\n   reference's behaviour-coverage checks (`get_behavior_per_interval`), plus rejection of\\n   trials with NaN in either continuous behaviour.\\n4. **Neural values**: raw spike counts stored as float32 (matching the reference's `ubyte` CSR\\n   cache). Standardisation is a model-side step in the reference and the provided decoder does\\n   its own SVD projection.\\n5. **Discretisation of continuous outputs**: per-session tertiles (33.3 / 66.7 percentiles) of the\\n   binned values pooled over all retained trials of that session, giving classes\\n   `low`/`medium`/`high`. Per-session rather than global because whisker motion energy is in\\n   arbitrary units that depend on camera, illumination and ROI size and is therefore not\\n   comparable across sessions; tertiles because the Decoder Task asks for 3 bins and balanced\\n   accuracy is the evaluation metric, so equal-frequency bins are the natural choice.\\n6. **Everything time-varying**: `input` and `output` are both `(d, 100)` per trial; per-trial\\n   quantities are broadcast across time, as the format instructions prefer.\\n7. **Session exclusion**: sessions from the 459-eid BWM freeze; dropped if no whisker motion\\n   energy is available, if no neuron survives curation, or if fewer than 2 trials survive.\\n\\n### Planned Sanity Checks\\n- [ ] #sessions ≈ 433 (method paper), #subjects ≤ 139, Beryl regions ≈ 270\\n- [ ] mean good neurons/session ≈ 75,708 / 459 ≈ 165 before grey-matter filtering\\n- [ ] T == 100 for every trial; `qc=None` ⇒ keep **all** clusters, `qc=1` ⇒ keep clusters with `label >= 1` (IBL \\\\\\\"good\\\\\\\"/well-isolated units) |\\\\n| `merge_probes(spikes_list, clusters_list)` | `ibl_data_utils.py` | LOADING | Concatenates probes of one session into one population, re-indexing `spikes['clusters']`, re-sorting spikes by time |\\\\n| `load_trials_and_mask(one, eid, min_rt=0.08, max_rt=2., nan_exclude='default', max_trial_len=10.0, exclude_nochoice=True)` | `ibl_data_utils.py` | CURATION | Returns full trials table + boolean mask of usable trials |\\\\n| `list_brain_regions` / `select_brain_regions` | `ibl_data_utils.py` | CURATION | Maps cluster `acronym` → **Beryl** atlas mapping, selects clusters in requested regions (`single_region=False` ⇒ all regions together) |\\\\n| `bin_spiking_data(reg_clu_ids, neural_df, trials_df, **params)` | `ibl_data_utils.py` | PROCESSING | Builds intervals `stimOn + (-0.5, 1.5)`, bins spikes at 20 ms via `bincount2D`, returns `(n_trials, T=100, n_clusters)` |\\\\n| `get_spike_data_per_interval` | `ibl_data_utils.py` | PROCESSING | Per-interval `bincount2D(times, clusters, xbin=0.02, xlim=[t_beg, t_end])`, keeps first `n_bins = ceil(2/0.02) = 100` columns |\\\\n| `load_target_behavior(one, eid, target)` | `ibl_data_utils.py` | LOADING | `SessionLoader.load_wheel()` → `wheel-speed` = `abs(velocity)`; `SessionLoader.load_motion_energy(views=['left'])` → `leftCamera.whiskerMotionEnergy` |\\\\n| `bin_behaviors(one, eid, behaviors, trials_df, **params)` | `ibl_data_utils.py` | PROCESSING | Per-trial: `choice`, `block` (= `probabilityLeft`), `reward` (`rewardVolume>1`), `contrast`; time-varying behaviours via `get_behavior_per_interval` |\\\\n| `get_behavior_per_interval` | `ibl_data_utils.py` | PROCESSING/CURATION | Slices behaviour samples inside each interval, linearly interpolates onto `np.linspace(t_beg + binsize, t_end, 100)`; marks interval bad if no samples, if it \\\\\\\"starts too late\\\\\\\"/\\\\\\\"ends too early\\\\\\\" (> 1 binsize gap at either edge), or if interval times are NaN |\\\\n| `align_spike_behavior(binned_spikes, binned_behaviors, beh_names, trials_mask)` | `ibl_data_utils.py` | CURATION | Drops trials failing the trials mask *or* missing any behaviour, keeping neural and behaviour trial-aligned |\\\\n| `standardize_spike_data` | `src/utils/data_loader_utils.py` | PROCESSING (model side) | Per-time-bin z-scoring; happens at model-fit time, **not** in the cached dataset |\\\\n| `create_dataset` | `src/utils/dataset_utils.py` | SAVING | Stores binned spikes as `np.ubyte` CSR — i.e. the cached neural data are **raw spike counts**, not rates |\\\\n\\\\n### Notes\\\\n- Answers to the checklist questions: this is **electrophysiology**, so no ΔF/F. Cell quality\\\\n  filtering *is* available (`load_spiking_data(qc=...)` on the IBL `label` metric) — see Step 4\\\\n  for the decision.\\\\n- `load_spiking_data` also calls `spike_loader.raw_electrophysiology(band=\\\\\\\"ap\\\\\\\", stream=True).fs`\\\\n  purely to record the AP sampling frequency in metadata. That streams raw binary from the\\\\n  remote server and is impossible (and pointless) offline — omitted.\\\\n- `SessionLoader` in the installed ibllib 4.0.1 is keyword-only (`SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid)`),\\\\n  while the 2025 reference code calls it positionally. Reference helpers are therefore called\\\\n  with an explicitly-constructed `sess_loader`.\\\\n- Example decoder outputs shipped with the reference code\\\\n  (`data/example_decoder_outputs/<eid>/<target>/<region>/metrics/fold_*.npy`) give per-fold\\\\n  metrics under four neuron-selection strategies: `all_ks`, `good_ks`, `thresholded`,\\\\n  `density_based`. Averaged over the 17 example sessions × 5 folds, region `all`:\\\\n\\\\n  | target | all_ks | good_ks | thresholded | density_based |\\\\n  |--------|--------|---------|-------------|---------------|\\\\n  | choice (AUC) | 0.896 | 0.869 | 0.879 | 0.884 |\\\\n  | prior (R²)   | 0.270 | 0.182 | 0.248 | 0.247 |\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 2: Dataset Exploration\\\\n**Status**: COMPLETE\\\\n\\\\n### Data Structure\\\\nONE cache, standard IBL ALF layout:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\n/app/data/one_cache/\\\\n  Brainwidemap/{sessions,datasets}.pqt      # release tables: 480 sessions, 76,563 datasets\\\\n  2022_Q4_IBL_et_al_BWM/…                   # 354 sessions\\\\n  2025_Q3_IBL_et_al_BWM/…                   # 459 sessions, 5,339 datasets (video revisions)\\\\n  .rest/                                    # 6,483 cached Alyx REST responses\\\\n  <lab>/Subjects/<subject>/<date>/<number>/alf/\\\\n      _ibl_trials.table.pqt, _ibl_trials.{goCueTrigger_times,stimOff_times}.npy\\\\n      _ibl_wheel.{position,timestamps}.npy\\\\n      {left,right}Camera.ROIMotionEnergy.npy, _ibl_{left,right}Camera.times.npy\\\\n      probe0N/pykilosort/{spikes.times,spikes.clusters,spikes.depths}.npy\\\\n                        {clusters.channels,clusters.depths,clusters.metrics.pqt}\\\\n                        channels.brainLocationIds_ccf_2017.npy\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nOnly the files needed for this analysis are staged (16 per session), not the full 76,563-dataset\\\\nrelease; everything is loaded through `ONE` / `brainbox` loaders, never by reading files directly.\\\\n\\\\nKey variables:\\\\n- `trials` table (20 columns): `stimOn_times`, `goCue_times`, `goCueTrigger_times`,\\\\n  `firstMovement_times`, `response_times`, `feedback_times`, `feedbackType`, `choice`,\\\\n  `contrastLeft`, `contrastRight`, `probabilityLeft`, `rewardVolume`, `intervals_0/1`,\\\\n  `stimOff_times`, `quiescencePeriod`, …\\\\n  - `choice ∈ {-1, 0, +1}`; verified empirically (see Step 4) that `choice == +1` is a **left**\\\\n    report and `choice == -1` a **right** report; `0` = no-go.\\\\n  - `probabilityLeft ∈ {0.2, 0.5, 0.8}`.\\\\n- `wheel`: `SessionLoader.load_wheel()` returns position interpolated to 1 kHz plus Gaussian-smoothed\\\\n  `velocity`/`acceleration`.\\\\n- `leftCamera.ROIMotionEnergy` (whisker motion energy) at ~60 Hz; `rightCamera` at ~150 Hz.\\\\n- clusters table after `merge_clusters`: IBL QC metrics (`amp_median`, `noise_cutoff`,\\\\n  `slidingRP_viol`, `label`, `firing_rate`, …) plus Allen `acronym` per cluster.\\\\n\\\\n### Dataset Size (from data files / release table)\\\\n| Statistic | Value |\\\\n|-----------|-------|\\\\n| Sessions (BWM freeze `bwm_release.csv`) | 459 |\\\\n| Probe insertions | 699 (701 probe dirs staged) |\\\\n| Subjects | 139 |\\\\n| Sessions / subject | 1–? (mean 3.3) |\\\\n| Session dirs staged | 461 |\\\\n| Sessions with `leftCamera.ROIMotionEnergy` | 439 |\\\\n| Sessions with `rightCamera.ROIMotionEnergy` | 422 |\\\\n| Clusters / probe (example sessions) | 898, 1728 (2 probes), 1202 (2 probes) |\\\\n| Good clusters (`label >= 1`) / session | 76, 264, 163 in the 3 probed examples |\\\\n| Trials / session (raw) | 565, 425, 557 in the same examples |\\\\n| Trials / session passing reference mask | 407, 244, 148 |\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 3: Reference Text Reading\\\\n**Status**: COMPLETE\\\\n\\\\n### Expected Statistics (from papers/methods)\\\\n| Statistic | Value | Source Quote |\\\\n|-----------|-------|--------------|\\\\n| Mice | 139 | \\\\\\\"We trained 139 mice (94 male and 45 female)\\\\\\\" (data paper) |\\\\n| Probes | 699 | \\\\\\\"we inserted 699 Neuropixels probes\\\\\\\" |\\\\n| Sessions released | 459 | \\\\\\\"a total of 459 sessions, 699 insertions and 621,733 neurons remained\\\\\\\" |\\\\n| Units (all Kilosort) | 621,733 (avg 889/probe) | \\\\\\\"This process produced 621,733 units (including multineuron activity), averaging 889 per probe\\\\\\\" |\\\\n| **Well-isolated neurons** | **75,708 (avg 108/probe)** | \\\\\\\"identified 75,708 well-isolated neurons, averaging 108 per probe\\\\\\\" |\\\\n| Sessions used by method paper | **433** | \\\\\\\"We apply our models to 433 IBL sessions, covering 270 brain regions\\\\\\\" |\\\\n| Brain regions | **270** | same |\\\\n| Trials/session floor | ≥250 (release), ≥400 (analyses) | \\\\\\\"mice performed at least 250 trials\\\\\\\"; \\\\\\\"Only sessions with at least 400 trials were retained\\\\\\\" |\\\\n| Neural data time bin | **20 ms**, T = **100** | \\\\\\\"Recordings are split into 2-s trials, each divided into 20-ms bins, producing T = 100 time steps\\\\\\\" |\\\\n| Behaviour sampling | 60 Hz (left cam) | \\\\\\\"wheel speed and whisker motion energy are time-varying signals sampled at 60 Hz\\\\\\\" |\\\\n| Alignment for choice | stimulus onset, −0.5 → +1.5 s | \\\\\\\"For choice, we align trials to the stimulus onset, considering neural activity from 0.5 s before to 1.5 s post-onset\\\\\\\" |\\\\n| Reward rate | ~0.85 (measured on example session) | task performance ≥90% on 100% contrast trials |\\\\n| Block structure | first 90 trials at 0.5; then 0.2/0.8 blocks of 20–100 trials, mean 51 | \\\\\\\"After an initial 90 unbiased trials… empirical mean of 51 trials\\\\\\\" |\\\\n| Contrast set | {0, 6.25, 12.5, 25, 100}% | data paper |\\\\n| Choice decoding (Zhang, region `all`) | AUC 0.90 (all units) / 0.87 (good units) | example decoder outputs |\\\\n| Prior decoding (Zhang, region `all`) | R² 0.27 / 0.18 | example decoder outputs |\\\\n\\\\n### Processing Details\\\\n- **Alignment**: `stimOn_times`, window `(-0.5, +1.5) s` ⇒ 2 s interval.\\\\n- **Binning**: 20 ms non-overlapping ⇒ T = 100. Spike bin `k` spans\\\\n  `[stimOn − 0.5 + 0.02k, stimOn − 0.5 + 0.02(k+1))` (this is exactly what `bincount2D`\\\\n  with `xlim=[t_beg,t_end]` does, and the reference then truncates to the first 100 columns).\\\\n- **Continuous behaviour**: linearly interpolated onto `t_beg + 0.02·(k+1)`, i.e. the **right edge**\\\\n  of each spike bin.\\\\n- The method paper also describes 50-ms bins in a −0.5/+1.5 s window for choice and a\\\\n  movement-aligned 0/+1 s window for the dynamic behaviours; the *released caching code*\\\\n  (which is what is reproducible and which produces one dataset carrying all four behaviours)\\\\n  uses the stimulus-onset 2 s / 20 ms / T=100 configuration, which is also the configuration\\\\n  stated in the paper's Results (\\\\\\\"2-s trials… 20-ms bins… T = 100\\\\\\\"). The Decoder Task here\\\\n  fixes stimulus-onset alignment, so that configuration is used.\\\\n\\\\n### Curation Steps\\\\n\\\\n**Neuron curation rules** (data paper \\\\\\\"Neurons and brain regions\\\\\\\"):\\\\n- Exclude units failing any of the three RIGOR single-unit metrics: amplitude > 50 µV,\\\\n  noise cut-off < 20 µV, refractory-period violation. Units passing all three are\\\\n  \\\\\\\"well-isolated neurons\\\\\\\" (75,708 of 621,733). In the IBL cluster table this is exactly\\\\n  `label >= 1` (`label` is the fraction of the three metrics passed: 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1).\\\\n- Analyses further restricted to **grey-matter** regions in the Allen CCF, with ≥5 neurons\\\\n  per session and recorded in ≥2 sessions.\\\\n\\\\n**Trial curation rules** (data paper \\\\\\\"Trials\\\\\\\", implemented in `load_trials_and_mask`):\\\\n- Exclude a trial if any of `stimOn_times`, `choice`, `feedback_times`, `probabilityLeft`,\\\\n  `firstMovement_times`, `feedbackType` is NaN.\\\\n- Exclude if reaction time (`firstMovement_times − stimOn_times`) ∉ [0.08, 2.00] s.\\\\n- Reference code adds `max_trial_len=10.0` (`feedback_times − goCue_times ≤ 10 s`) and\\\\n  `exclude_nochoice=True` (`choice != 0`).\\\\n\\\\n### Decoders Trained (reference)\\\\n| Decoded variable | Metric | Reference value (region `all`) |\\\\n|------------------|--------|-------------------------------|\\\\n| choice | AUC | 0.896 (all units) / 0.869 (good units) |\\\\n| prior | R² | 0.270 / 0.182 |\\\\n| wheel speed | R² | reported only in figures (single-trial R², ≈0.4–0.6) |\\\\n| whisker motion energy | R² | reported only in figures (≈0.5–0.7) |\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 4: Check for Consistency\\\\n**Status**: COMPLETE\\\\n\\\\n### Discrepancies Found\\\\n| Topic | Code says | Data shows | Papers say | Resolution |\\\\n|-------|-----------|------------|------------|------------|\\\\n| Neuron quality filter | `load_spiking_data(qc=None)` ⇒ **all** Kilosort clusters | `label>=1` selects ~8–15% of clusters (76/898, 264/1728, 163/1202) | Method paper: \\\\\\\"bin spike counts using **all neurons**, sorted by Kilosort 2.5\\\\\\\"; data paper: analyses restricted to the **75,708 well-isolated neurons** | **Use well-isolated neurons (`label >= 1`)**. Rationale below. |\\\\n| Brain-region set | `list_brain_regions` keeps every Beryl acronym incl. `root`/`void`; `MultiRegionDataModule` drops `root`/`void` | 15–20% of good clusters map to `root`/`void` | Data paper restricts to Allen **grey matter** | Drop `root`/`void` (non-grey-matter / unassigned), keep everything else. Gives a Beryl region list comparable to the paper's 270 regions. |\\\\n| Time bin | code: 20 ms, T=100 | — | Results: 20 ms, T=100; STAR Methods \\\\\\\"data processing\\\\\\\": 50 ms for choice/prior, 20 ms for dynamic behaviours | Use **20 ms, T = 100**: it matches the released code and the Results text, and the Decoder Task requires one common binning for all four outputs. |\\\\n| Alignment | code: `stimOn_times` | — | STAR Methods uses `firstMovement_times` for the dynamic behaviours | Use **`stimOn_times`** — mandated by the Decoder Task and by the released caching code. |\\\\n| `allow_nans` for behaviours | reference passes `allow_nans=True` and later imputes NaNs with the trial mean inside the data loader | motion energy occasionally has NaN runs | — | Drop trials whose wheel-speed or whisker-ME window contains NaN. The target format forbids NaN, and imputing a value then discretising it would fabricate labels. |\\\\n| Sessions | freeze file lists 459 eids | 461 session dirs staged | Method paper used **433** sessions | Start from the 459-eid freeze, drop sessions with no usable whisker video, no surviving neurons, or <2 usable trials; expect to land near 433. |\\\\n| `choice` sign | code stores raw `choice` | on 100%-contrast trials: stim-left ⇒ `choice=+1` in 71/72 trials, stim-right ⇒ `choice=−1` in 61/63 | mice report the stimulus side | `choice == +1` ⇒ **left** report ⇒ label 0; `choice == −1` ⇒ **right** report ⇒ label 1. |\\\\n\\\\n**Why well-isolated neurons rather than \\\\\\\"all neurons\\\\\\\":**\\\\n1. The data paper — the source of these data — explicitly defines its analysis population as the\\\\n   75,708 well-isolated neurons and excludes the rest as multi-unit activity.\\\\n2. The reference code exposes exactly this switch (`qc=1` ⇒ `label >= 1`) and its `merge_probes`\\\\n   docstring is written against `brainwidemap.load_good_units`.\\\\n3. Feasibility: all 621,733 units at T=100 × ~300 usable trials × 459 sessions would be ≈120 GB of\\\\n   float32 — not a storable/trainable dataset. Well-isolated units give ≈8 GB.\\\\n4. Cost is small and quantified: the reference's own example outputs show choice AUC 0.896 with\\\\n   all units vs 0.869 with good units (−3%).\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 5: Mapping Planning\\\\n**Status**: COMPLETE\\\\n\\\\n### Variable Mapping\\\\n| Source Variable | Target Field | Transform | Reference Code Function(s) | Notes |\\\\n|-----------------|--------------|-----------|----------------------------|-------|\\\\n| `spikes.times`, `spikes.clusters` (all probes, merged) | `neural[s][k]` (n_neurons, 100) float32 | spike counts in 20 ms bins over `stimOn + [-0.5, 1.5)` | `merge_probes`, `bin_spiking_data`/`bincount2D` | raw counts, no rate conversion, no z-scoring (reference z-scores inside the model's data loader, not in the cached data) |\\\\n| bin right-edge time relative to `stimOn_times` | `input[s][k][0, :]` | `-0.5 + 0.02·(k+1)` ∈ [−0.48, 1.50] | `get_behavior_per_interval`'s `x_interp` grid | \\\\\\\"time since stimulus onset\\\\\\\", continuous, time-varying |\\\\n| index of the trial within its `probabilityLeft` block | `input[s][k][1, :]` | 0-based count from block start, computed on the **unfiltered** trials table, broadcast over T | — (new; required by Decoder Task) | \\\\\\\"trial number in block\\\\\\\", continuous, per-trial → broadcast to time-varying |\\\\n| `trials.choice` | `output[s][k][0, :]` | `+1 → 0` (left), `−1 → 1` (right); broadcast over T | `bin_behaviors` (`choice`) | binary, per-trial |\\\\n| `trials.probabilityLeft` | `output[s][k][1, :]` | `0.2→0, 0.5→1, 0.8→2`; broadcast over T | `bin_behaviors` (`block`) | 3-way, per-trial |\\\\n| `SessionLoader.wheel.velocity` | `output[s][k][2, :]` | `abs(velocity)` → interp to bin edges → per-session tertiles → {0,1,2} | `load_target_behavior('wheel-speed')`, `get_behavior_per_interval` | time-varying |\\\\n| `leftCamera.ROIMotionEnergy` (fallback `rightCamera`) | `output[s][k][3, :]` | interp to bin edges → per-session tertiles → {0,1,2} | `load_target_behavior('left-whisker-motion-energy')` | time-varying |\\\\n| `clusters.acronym` → Beryl | `brain_region_idx[s]`, `brain_regions` | `BrainRegions().acronym2acronym(..., 'Beryl')` | `list_brain_regions` | `root`/`void` dropped |\\\\n| `bwm_release.csv` `subject` | `subjects`, `subject_idx` | unique sorted list | — | |\\\\n\\\\n### Key Decisions\\\\n1. **Alignment / window / binning**: `stimOn_times`, `(-0.5, +1.5) s`, 20 ms ⇒ T = 100.\\\\n   Exactly the reference `params`; also required by the Decoder Task.\\\\n2. **Neuron curation**: IBL `label >= 1` (all three RIGOR metrics passed) **and** Beryl region\\\\n   ∉ {`root`, `void`}. Sessions are merged across probes first (`merge_probes`), as the reference\\\\n   and the data paper both do (\\\\\\\"neurons in the same session and region were combined across probes\\\\\\\").\\\\n   The data paper's extra region criteria (≥5 neurons/session, region seen in ≥2 sessions) are\\\\n   *not* applied: they exist to make region-wise statistical maps comparable, whereas here every\\\\n   session is decoded from its whole population, and applying them would delete neurons that\\\\n   carry signal for a session-level decoder.\\\\n3. **Trial curation**: `load_trials_and_mask(min_rt=0.08, max_rt=2.0, nan_exclude='default',\\\\n   max_trial_len=10.0, exclude_nochoice=True)` — the reference call verbatim — plus the\\\\n   reference's behaviour-coverage checks (`get_behavior_per_interval`), plus rejection of\\\\n   trials with NaN in either continuous behaviour.\\\\n4. **Neural values**: raw spike counts stored as float32 (matching the reference's `ubyte` CSR\\\\n   cache). Standardisation is a model-side step in the reference and the provided decoder does\\\\n   its own SVD projection.\\\\n5. **Discretisation of continuous outputs**: per-session tertiles (33.3 / 66.7 percentiles) of the\\\\n   binned values pooled over all retained trials of that session, giving classes\\\\n   `low`/`medium`/`high`. Per-session rather than global because whisker motion energy is in\\\\n   arbitrary units that depend on camera, illumination and ROI size and is therefore not\\\\n   comparable across sessions; tertiles because the Decoder Task asks for 3 bins and balanced\\\\n   accuracy is the evaluation metric, so equal-frequency bins are the natural choice.\\\\n6. **Everything time-varying**: `input` and `output` are both `(d, 100)` per trial; per-trial\\\\n   quantities are broadcast across time, as the format instructions prefer.\\\\n7. **Session exclusion**: sessions from the 459-eid BWM freeze; dropped if no whisker motion\\\\n   energy is available, if no neuron survives curation, or if fewer than 2 trials survive.\\\\n\\\\n### Planned Sanity Checks\\\\n- [ ] #sessions ≈ 433 (method paper), #subjects ≤ 139, Beryl regions ≈ 270\\\\n- [ ] mean good neurons/session ≈ 75,708 / 459 ≈ 165 before grey-matter filtering\\\\n- [ ] T == 100 for every trial; `input[0]` range == [−0.48, 1.50]\\\\n- [ ] choice class balance near 50/50; prior classes ≈ {0.2: 0.42, 0.5: 0.16, 0.8: 0.42}\\\\n- [ ] wheel-speed and whisker-ME class fractions ≈ 1/3 each by construction\\\\n- [ ] spike counts non-negative integers; mean firing rate per neuron in a plausible 0.1–50 Hz range\\\\n- [ ] independent re-derivation of one trial's spike counts, input, and each output from\\\\n      freshly loaded ONE objects (`np.allclose`) — Step 10\\\\n- [ ] trial-in-block resets exactly at `probabilityLeft` changes and the first block has 90 trials\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 6: Script Development\\\\n**Status**: NOT Spike bin `k` spans\\n  `[stimOn − 0.5 + 0.02k, stimOn − 0.5 + 0.02(k+1))` (this is exactly what `bincount2D`\\n  with `xlim=[t_beg,t_end]` does, and the reference then truncates to the first 100 columns).\\n- **Continuous behaviour**: linearly interpolated onto `t_beg + 0.02·(k+1)`, i.e. the **right edge**\\n  of each spike bin.\\n- The method paper also describes 50-ms bins in a −0.5/+1.5 s window for choice and a\\n  movement-aligned 0/+1 s window for the dynamic behaviours; the *released caching code*\\n  (which is what is reproducible and which produces one dataset carrying all four behaviours)\\n  uses the stimulus-onset 2 s / 20 ms / T=100 configuration, which is also the configuration\\n  stated in the paper's Results (\\\"2-s trials… 20-ms bins… T = 100\\\"). The Decoder Task here\\n  fixes stimulus-onset alignment, so that configuration is used.\\n\\n### Curation Steps\\n\\n**Neuron curation rules** (data paper \\\"Neurons and brain regions\\\"):\\n- Exclude units failing any of the three RIGOR single-unit metrics: amplitude > 50 µV,\\n  noise cut-off < 20 µV, refractory-period violation. Units passing all three are\\n  \\\"well-isolated neurons\\\" (75,708 of 621,733). In the IBL cluster table this is exactly\\n  `label >= 1` (`label` is the fraction of the three metrics passed: 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1).\\n- Analyses further restricted to **grey-matter** regions in the Allen CCF, with ≥5 neurons\\n  per session and recorded in ≥2 sessions.\\n\\n**Trial curation rules** (data paper \\\"Trials\\\", implemented in `load_trials_and_mask`):\\n- Exclude a trial if any of `stimOn_times`, `choice`, `feedback_times`, `probabilityLeft`,\\n  `firstMovement_times`, `feedbackType` is NaN.\\n- Exclude if reaction time (`firstMovement_times − stimOn_times`) ∉ [0.08, 2.00] s.\\n- Reference code adds `max_trial_len=10.0` (`feedback_times − goCue_times ≤ 10 s`) and\\n  `exclude_nochoice=True` (`choice != 0`).\\n\\n### Decoders Trained (reference)\\n| Decoded variable | Metric | Reference value (region `all`) |\\n|------------------|--------|-------------------------------|\\n| choice | AUC | 0.896 (all units) / 0.869 (good units) |\\n| prior | R² | 0.270 / 0.182 |\\n| wheel speed | R² | reported only in figures (single-trial R², ≈0.4–0.6) |\\n| whisker motion energy | R² | reported only in figures (≈0.5–0.7) |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Step 4: Check for Consistency\\n**Status**: COMPLETE\\n\\n### Discrepancies Found\\n| Topic | Code says | Data shows | Papers say | Resolution |\\n|-------|-----------|------------|------------|------------|\\n| Neuron quality filter | `load_spiking_data(qc=None)` ⇒ **all** Kilosort clusters | `label>=1` selects ~8–15% of clusters (76/898, 264/1728, 163/1202) | Method paper: \\\"bin spike counts using **all neurons**, sorted by Kilosort 2.5\\\"; data paper: analyses restricted to the **75,708 well-isolated neurons** | **Use well-isolated neurons (`label >= 1`)**. Rationale below. |\\n| Brain-region set | `list_brain_regions` keeps every Beryl acronym incl. `root`/`void`; `MultiRegionDataModule` drops `root`/`void` | 15–20% of good clusters map to `root`/`void` | Data paper restricts to Allen **grey matter** | Drop `root`/`void` (non-grey-matter / unassigned), keep everything else. Gives a Beryl region list comparable to the paper's 270 regions. |\\n| Time bin | code: 20 ms, T=100 | — | Results: 20 ms, T=100; STAR Methods \\\"data processing\\\": 50 ms for choice/prior, 20 ms for dynamic behaviours | Use **20 ms, T = 100**: it matches the released code and the Results text, and the Decoder Task requires one common binning for all four outputs. |\\n| Alignment | code: `stimOn_times` | — | STAR Methods uses `firstMovement_times` for the dynamic behaviours | Use **`stimOn_times`** — mandated by the Decoder Task and by the released caching code. |\\n| `allow_nans` for behaviours | reference passes `allow_nans=True` and later imputes NaNs with the trial mean inside the data loader | motion energy occasionally has NaN runs | — | Drop trials whose wheel-speed or whisker-ME window contains NaN. The target format forbids NaN, and imputing a value then discretising it would fabricate labels. |\\n| Sessions | freeze file lists 459 eids | 461 session dirs staged | Method paper used **433** sessions | Start from the 459-eid freeze, drop sessions with no usable whisker video, no surviving neurons, or <2 usable trials; expect to land near 433. |\\n| `choice` sign | code stores raw `choice` | on 100%-contrast trials: stim-left ⇒ `choice=+1` in 71/72 trials, stim-right ⇒ `choice=−1` in 61/63 | mice report the stimulus side | `choice == +1` ⇒ **left** report ⇒ label 0; `choice == −1` ⇒ **right** report ⇒ label 1. |\\n\\n**Why well-isolated neurons rather than \\\"all neurons\\\":**\\n1. The data paper — the source of these data — explicitly defines its analysis population as the\\n   75,708 well-isolated neurons and excludes the rest as multi-unit activity.\\n2. The reference code exposes exactly this switch (`qc=1` ⇒ `label >= 1`) and its `merge_probes`\\n   docstring is written against `brainwidemap.load_good_units`.\\n3. Feasibility: all 621,733 units at T=100 × ~300 usable trials × 459 sessions would be ≈120 GB of\\n   float32 — not a storable/trainable dataset. Well-isolated units give ≈8 GB.\\n4. Cost is small and quantified: the reference's own example outputs show choice AUC 0.896 with\\n   all units vs 0.869 with good units (−3%).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Step 5: Mapping Planning\\n**Status**: COMPLETE\\n\\n### Variable Mapping\\n| Source Variable | Target Field | Transform | Reference Code Function(s) | Notes |\\n|-----------------|--------------|-----------|----------------------------|-------|\\n| `spikes.times`, `spikes.clusters` (all probes, merged) | `neural[s][k]` (n_neurons, 100) float32 | spike counts in 20 ms bins over `stimOn + [-0.5, 1.5)` | `merge_probes`, `bin_spiking_data`/`bincount2D` | raw counts, no rate conversion, no z-scoring (reference z-scores inside the model's data loader, not in the cached data) |\\n| bin right-edge time relative to `stimOn_times` | `input[s][k][0, :]` | `-0.5 + 0.02·(k+1)` ∈ [−0.48, 1.50] | `get_behavior_per_interval`'s `x_interp` grid | \\\"time since stimulus onset\\\", continuous, time-varying |\\n| index of the trial within its `probabilityLeft` block | `input[s][k][1, :]` | 0-based count from block start, computed on the **unfiltered** trials table, broadcast over T | — (new; required by Decoder Task) | \\\"trial number in block\\\", continuous, per-trial → broadcast to time-varying |\\n| `trials.choice` | `output[s][k][0, :]` | `+1 → 0` (left), `−1 → 1` (right); broadcast over T | `bin_behaviors` (`choice`) | binary, per-trial |\\n| `trials.probabilityLeft` | `output[s][k][1, :]` | `0.2→0, 0.5→1, 0.8→2`; broadcast over T | `bin_behaviors` (`block`) | 3-way, per-trial |\\n| `SessionLoader.wheel.velocity` | `output[s][k][2, :]` | `abs(velocity)` → interp to bin edges → per-session tertiles → {0,1,2} | `load_target_behavior('wheel-speed')`, `get_behavior_per_interval` | time-varying |\\n| `leftCamera.ROIMotionEnergy` (fallback `rightCamera`) | `output[s][k][3, :]` | interp to bin edges → per-session tertiles → {0,1,2} | `load_target_behavior('left-whisker-motion-energy')` | time-varying |\\n| `clusters.acronym` → Beryl | `brain_region_idx[s]`, `brain_regions` | `BrainRegions().acronym2acronym(..., 'Beryl')` | `list_brain_regions` | `root`/`void` dropped |\\n| `bwm_release.csv` `subject` | `subjects`, `subject_idx` | unique sorted list | — | |\\n\\n### Key Decisions\\n1. **Alignment / window / binning**: `stimOn_times`, `(-0.5, +1.5) s`, 20 ms ⇒ T = 100.\\n   Exactly the reference `params`; also required by the Decoder Task.\\n2. **Neuron curation**: IBL `label >= 1` (all three RIGOR metrics passed) **and** Beryl region\\n   ∉ {`root`, `void`}. Sessions are merged across probes first (`merge_probes`), as the reference\\n   and the data paper both do (\\\"neurons in the same session and region were combined across probes\\\").\\n   The data paper's extra region criteria (≥5 neurons/session, region seen in ≥2 sessions) are\\n   *not* applied: they exist to make region-wise statistical maps comparable, whereas here every\\n   session is decoded from its whole population, and applying them would delete neurons that\\n   carry signal for a session-level decoder.\\n3. **Trial curation**: `load_trials_and_mask(min_rt=0.08, max_rt=2.0, nan_exclude='default',\\n   max_trial_len=10.0, exclude_nochoice=True)` — the reference call verbatim — plus the\\n   reference's behaviour-coverage checks (`get_behavior_per_interval`), plus rejection of\\n   trials with NaN in either continuous behaviour.\\n4. **Neural values**: raw spike counts stored as float32 (matching the reference's `ubyte` CSR\\n   cache). Standardisation is a model-side step in the reference and the provided decoder does\\n   its own SVD projection.\\n5. **Discretisation of continuous outputs**: per-session tertiles (33.3 / 66.7 percentiles) of the\\n   binned values pooled over all retained trials of that session, giving classes\\n   `low`/`medium`/`high`. Per-session rather than global because whisker motion energy is in\\n   arbitrary units that depend on camera, illumination and ROI size and is therefore not\\n   comparable across sessions; tertiles because the Decoder Task asks for 3 bins and balanced\\n   accuracy is the evaluation metric, so equal-frequency bins are the natural choice.\\n6. **Everything time-varying**: `input` and `output` are both `(d, 100)` per trial; per-trial\\n   quantities are broadcast across time, as the format instructions prefer.\\n7. **Session exclusion**: sessions from the 459-eid BWM freeze; dropped if no whisker motion\\n   energy is available, if no neuron survives curation, or if fewer than 2 trials survive.\\n\\n### Planned Sanity Checks\\n- [ ] #sessions ≈ 433 (method paper), #subjects ≤ 139, Beryl regions ≈ 270\\n- [ ] mean good neurons/session ≈ 75,708 / 459 ≈ 165 before grey-matter filtering\\n- [ ] T == 100 for every trial; `input[0]` range == [−0.48, 1.50]\\n- [ ] choice class balance near 50/50; prior classes ≈ {0.2: 0.42, 0.5: 0.16, 0.8: 0.42}\\n- [ ] wheel-speed and whisker-ME class fractions ≈ 1/3 each by construction\\n- [ ] spike counts non-negative integers; mean firing rate per neuron in a plausible 0.1–50 Hz range\\n- [ ] independent re-derivation of one trial's spike counts, input, and each output from\\n      freshly loaded ONE objects (`np.allclose`) — Step 10\\n- [
